Component reference

Every M3e.* module, its overview, and every exposed value — extracted from the library source at build time.

Two forms

Every component is reachable two ways — same output, different import and different strictness:

  • The barrel (import M3e) — one import for everything. M3e.button, M3e.icon, and the shared M3e.Attributes.variant Value.filled vocabulary. This is the form the Guide teaches; it's the generic, easy form.
  • The component module (import M3e.Button) — M3e.Component.Button.component and its component-scoped M3e.Component.Button.variant / slot setters (M3e.Component.Button.icon). More precise: the compiler rejects a token or slot child that isn't valid for that component.

Barrel-vs-module isn't a surface choice and it isn't an escape hatch — it's a separate axis, only which import you reach through. Start on the barrel; reach for a component module when you want the tighter, component-scoped types.

M3e · the barrel

The general surface: every component constructor in the elm/html call shape, one import. Signatures reference each component's aliases — reach for `M3e.<Component>` when you want the strict per-component surface (required content, builder, narrowed values), and `M3e.Attributes` / `M3e.Events` / `M3e.Values` for the shared vocabulary.

`toHtml` is the render bridge to `elm/html`.

The `slot<Name>` placers assign a child element to a named slot in any component that accepts it. Admittance is open (broad row) — wrong-kind placements are caught by `Cem.ValidSlotKind` (elm-review).

Component constructors (150)
type Element

The typed IR element every constructor here produces. Re-exported so callers never import `HtmlIr.Element` directly.

type Attr

A typed attribute. Re-exported so callers never import `HtmlIr.Attribute` directly.

type Node

The untyped IR node an `Element` wraps — the erased form, carrying no phantom claims. Re-exported for the boundaries that must store renderable content in a monomorphic field (a framework `View` record, a cache); lift it back with `<Lib>.Unsafe.fromNode`.

text : String.String -> M3e.Element { s | sharedText : HtmlIr.Kind.Shared } admittedBy msg

The shared text atom — admissible into any library's opted-in slot.

toHtml : M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> Html.Html msg

Render any element from this library to `elm/html`.

toNode : M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Node msg

Erase an element to its untyped [`Node`](#Node) — the safe out-bound direction; the phantom rows are discarded, never re-asserted.

mapMsg : (a -> b) -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy a -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy b

Map the `msg` type of any element from this library (the typed IR's `Html.map`). Structural: the tree is not rendered, rows are preserved.

mapNode : (a -> b) -> M3e.Node a -> M3e.Node b

[`mapMsg`](#mapMsg) for an erased [`Node`](#Node).

key : String.String -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Attach a diff key to a child so its parent container renders as a keyed node. State and animations survive reorders, insertions, and removals. Phantom rows are preserved — a keyed chip is still a chip.

lazy : (a -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Memoise a subtree while its input is referentially unchanged. The result keeps its phantom rows and drops into any slot. **The view function must be a stable top-level binding** — an inline lambda allocates a fresh closure each render and silently never memoises.

lazy2 : (a -> b -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

2-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy3 : (a -> b -> c -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

3-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy4 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

4-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy5 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

5-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy6 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

6-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy). Note type params skip `f` to match the underlying `VirtualDom.lazy6` convention.

lazy7 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

7-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy8 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> i -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> i -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

8-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy). **This variant does not memoise** — the Element→Html bridge only has room for seven memoised data arguments, so the eighth forces a fresh closure each render and defeats the reference check. For real memoisation, fold the extra state into one of the first seven arguments and use [`lazy7`](#lazy7).

addClass : String.String -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Add a CSS class, participating in the `class` merge. Phantom rows preserved.

when : Basics.Bool -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Keep an element only when the flag is `True`; `False` collapses it to an empty node that renders nothing. Phantom rows preserved.

testId : String.String -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Stamp a `data-testid` attribute for test hooks. Phantom rows preserved.

M3e.Action

Behavioural actions: exactly one of the supported behaviours, consumed by a component's `component`/`build` required record. Attribute behaviours (`onClick`/`link`/`remove`) become host attributes; wrapper behaviours nest the content in their trigger element.

type Action

An opaque behavioural value: exactly one of the supported behaviours.

type LinkSpec

The parts of a link action.

type BottomSheetSpec

The parts of a bottom-sheet trigger.

link : String.String -> M3e.Action.Action { c | link : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

A link action pointing at `url`.

linkWith : M3e.Action.LinkSpec -> M3e.Action.Action { c | link : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

A link action from a full `LinkSpec`.

none : M3e.Action.Action capability msg

No behaviour.

A click action: emit `msg` on activation.

A remove action: emit `msg` when the element requests removal.

M3e.Attributes

The canonical shared attribute vocabulary. Every setter is an open producer (`{ c | attr : Supported }`); each element's closed `Attrs` row decides admittance. Enum setters here close over the library-wide UNION of values — cross-component misuse is caught by elm-review; reach for the per-component setters (`M3e.<Component>.<attr>`) for compile-tight narrowing.

Portmanteau setters (`variantRainbow`, `shapeRounded`, …) are nullary aliases that pre-apply one enum token. They exist for IDE discovery: type `variant` and autocomplete lists every value inline. Each claims the same capability row as its base enum setter, so admittance is identical.

class : String.String -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | class : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

The global `class` attribute. Repeats ACCUMULATE: `[ class "a", class "b" ]` renders `class="a b"`.

id : String.String -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | id : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

The global `id` attribute.

slot : String.String -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | slot : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

The global `slot` attribute (named-slot placement by hand).

style : String.String -> String.String -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | style : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

One inline-style declaration (the `elm/html` 0.19 shape). Declarations MERGE across every `style` / `styleList` on the element, last-wins per property.

classList : List.List ( String.String, Basics.Bool ) -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | class : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

The classes whose flag is `True`, space-joined. Accumulates with every other `class` / `classList` on the element.

styleList : List.List ( String.String, String.String ) -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | style : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

Inline-style declarations as a `( property, value )` list (the `elm/html` 0.18 shape). Merges exactly as `style` does.

CAVEAT — this setter cannot RESYNC. `elm/virtual-dom` only re-forces an unchanged controlled property for the names `value` and `checked`; `selected` is compared by identity, so re-rendering the same model value after the user has changed it through the element's own UI will NOT push it back to the DOM. M3e.Build

The shared builder surface for the `M3e` brand: the opaque `Builder` and the single `toElement` that closes any component's builder. Per-component modules provide the seeds (`build`) and the narrowed `withX` setters; they all share this one representation, so `toElement` is defined once (in `M3e.Forge.Internal`) and re-exported here.

The `Is` aliases (`ButtonIs`, `CardIs`, …) let you annotate a phantom-kind type without importing the component or its builder module.

type Builder

The shared pipe-builder — see each component's `Builder` alias for its narrowed, brand-typed form.

type AccordionIs

The `Accordion` kind phantom — annotate with `List (Element (AccordionIs s) admittedBy msg)`.

A fractional value, between 0 and `max`, indicating progress. (default: `0`)

Sets the LIVE DOM property `value`, not the content attribute. The content attribute — the element's INITIAL state, and the only form that serializes to server-rendered markup — is `defaultValue`.

defaultValue : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | value : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

Set the `value` CONTENT attribute — the element's DEFAULT/initial `value`, mirroring HTML's own `defaultValue` IDL attribute. Unlike `value` (which writes the live DOM property) this one SERIALIZES: it is what server-rendered markup and `outerHTML` show, and it is what a form reset restores to.

A fractional value, between 0 and `max`, indicating progress. (default: `0`)

Sets the LIVE DOM property `value`, not the content attribute. The content attribute — the element's INITIAL state, and the only form that serializes to server-rendered markup — is `defaultValue`.

defaultValue : Basics.Float -> HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr { c | value : HtmlIr.Kind.Supported } msg

Set the `value` CONTENT attribute — the element's DEFAULT/initial `value`, mirroring HTML's own `defaultValue` IDL attribute. Unlike `value` (which writes the live DOM property) this one SERIALIZES: it is what server-rendered markup and `outerHTML` show, and it is what a form reset restores to.

M3e.Events

Events as capabilities: each setter is an open producer admitted only by elements whose closed `Attrs` row lists the event — `onClick` on a non-interactive element is a compile error.

`delegate` is the ONE loud escape for bubbling: it forgets an event's capability so it can be placed on a container and rely on DOM bubbling from an interactive descendant. Pair it with a real interactive child and a keyboard path (lint-checked).

M3e.Html

The loose, elm/html-like producer layer: one open-rowed constructor per element, each owning `Ir.node "<tag>"`. This is the foundation the `M3e-html` package exposes; every rich `M3e.<Component>` imports its producer here and re-exposes it under a tightened signature. Depends only on the IR substrate — no component module is imported.

The substrate types are re-exported here too, so a consumer of the published package can write type annotations without importing `HtmlIr.*` directly.

type Element

The typed IR element every constructor here produces. Re-exported so callers never import `HtmlIr.Element` directly.

type Attr

A typed attribute. Re-exported so callers never import `HtmlIr.Attribute` directly.

type Node

The untyped IR node an `Element` wraps — the erased form, carrying no phantom claims. Re-exported for the boundaries that must store renderable content in a monomorphic field (a framework `View` record, a cache); lift it back with `<Lib>.Unsafe.fromNode`.

toHtml : M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> Html.Html msg

Render any element from this library to `elm/html`.

toNode : M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Node msg

Erase an element to its untyped [`Node`](#Node) — the safe out-bound direction; the phantom rows are discarded, never re-asserted.

mapMsg : (a -> b) -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy a -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy b

Map the `msg` type of any element from this library (the typed IR's `Html.map`). Structural: the tree is not rendered, rows are preserved.

mapNode : (a -> b) -> M3e.Html.Node a -> M3e.Html.Node b

[`mapMsg`](#mapMsg) for an erased [`Node`](#Node).

key : String.String -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Attach a diff key to a child so its parent container renders as a keyed node. State and animations survive reorders, insertions, and removals. Phantom rows are preserved — a keyed chip is still a chip.

lazy : (a -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Memoise a subtree while its input is referentially unchanged. The result keeps its phantom rows and drops into any slot. **The view function must be a stable top-level binding** — an inline lambda allocates a fresh closure each render and silently never memoises.

lazy2 : (a -> b -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

2-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy3 : (a -> b -> c -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

3-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy4 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

4-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy5 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

5-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy6 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

6-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy). Note type params skip `f` to match the underlying `VirtualDom.lazy6` convention.

lazy7 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

7-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy).

lazy8 : (a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> i -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg) -> a -> b -> c -> d -> e -> g -> h -> i -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

8-argument variant of [`lazy`](#lazy). **This variant does not memoise** — the Element→Html bridge only has room for seven memoised data arguments, so the eighth forces a fresh closure each render and defeats the reference check. For real memoisation, fold the extra state into one of the first seven arguments and use [`lazy7`](#lazy7).

addClass : String.String -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Add a CSS class, participating in the `class` merge. Phantom rows preserved.

attrIf : Basics.Bool -> M3e.Html.Attr capability msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Conditionally attach an attribute — applied when the flag is `True`, a no-op when `False`. Phantom rows preserved.

when : Basics.Bool -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Keep an element only when the flag is `True`; `False` collapses it to an empty node that renders nothing. Phantom rows preserved.

testId : String.String -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg -> M3e.Html.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Stamp a `data-testid` attribute for test hooks. Phantom rows preserved.

M3e.Kind

The library's private phantom markers and named kind/context sets.

`Brand` marks this library's kind-row fields; `Ctx` marks its context-row fields. Both are nominal and private to this library — a foreign library's markers never unify with them, even under the same field name. `Available`/`Used` are the pipe-builder's write-once capability markers.

`Supported` and `Shared` are the CROSS-library markers, re-exported from the IR substrate so callers never import `HtmlIr.Kind` directly. Unlike `Brand`/`Ctx` these are deliberately shared: every brand's `Supported` is the same type, and a `Shared`-marked atom is admissible into any brand's opted-in slot.

type Brand

The private kind marker (never constructed).

type Ctx

The private context marker (never constructed).

type Available

Pipe-builder capability: still writable.

type Used

Pipe-builder capability: consumed.

type Supported

Admission marker for capability and value rows. Re-exported from `HtmlIr.Kind`.

type Shared

The cross-library atom marker. Re-exported from `HtmlIr.Kind`.

M3e.Unsafe

THE loud legacy-interop escapes: wrap raw `Html` as an `Element`, re-assert rows on an erased `Node`, re-kind an existing `Element`, or forge an element from a tag name this library has no generated producer for — all with FREE phantom rows, so the compiler checks nothing about the result. For incremental migration and slot-fit only; every use site is a grep target and a lint finding.

fromHtml : Html.Html msg -> HtmlIr.Element.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Wrap raw `Html` with FREE rows. Loud on purpose.

fromNode : HtmlIr.Node.Node msg -> HtmlIr.Element.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Re-assert FREE rows on an erased [`Node`](HtmlIr-Node#Node) — the exact dual of the safe `HtmlIr.Element.toNode`. For the boundary where a typed tree was flattened to the IR and must be lifted back (a framework `View` record, a cache). Loud on purpose: the rows it re-asserts were never checked.

recast : HtmlIr.Element.Element aAccepts aAdmittedBy msg -> HtmlIr.Element.Element bAccepts bAdmittedBy msg

Re-kind an `Element` to FREE rows so it fits any slot — the blessed form of the hand-forged `Ir.fromNode << HtmlIr.Element.toNode` recast. Loud on purpose.

recastAll : List.List (HtmlIr.Element.Element aAccepts aAdmittedBy msg) -> List.List (HtmlIr.Element.Element bAccepts bAdmittedBy msg)

`recast` mapped over a list of elements.

customElement : String.String -> List.List (HtmlIr.Attribute.Attr capability msg) -> List.List (HtmlIr.Element.Element childAccepts childAdmittedBy msg) -> HtmlIr.Element.Element accepts admittedBy msg

Forge an element from a raw tag name, with FREE rows — for a CUSTOM ELEMENT this library has no generated producer for (`<model-viewer>`, `<slide-panels>`). Loud on purpose: for a standard HTML tag reach for the native brand's typed constructor instead, and for a component this library already ships, use that.

M3e.Values

The enum-value vocabulary: every token minted once (open row), plus the library-wide union row per enum attribute, plus attribute-prefixed portmanteaus (`variantFilled`, `shapeRounded`, …) for IDE discovery. General setters close over the union; per-component setters narrow — both are fed by these same tokens.

`Value` is re-exported here so annotating a token never requires an `HtmlIr.Value` import.

type Value

The phantom-tagged enum token. Re-exported so callers never import `HtmlIr.Value` directly.

Advanced

Motion durations and state-layer opacities — raw CSS custom-property overrides for the 16 transition-timing tokens and 3 interaction-state opacity tokens @m3e/web exposes.

CSS Variables

Non-color @m3e/web CSS custom properties (typescale, shape, motion, state), grouped by name hierarchy. Color tokens live in the Color section. Type a value to override it; clear it to revert. Live default values are not shown — Elm cannot read computed CSS variables.
